title: Merciful and gracious (Exodus 34:6–7)
hookLine: the name proclaimed: merciful, gracious, slow to anger, abundant in steadfast love

lines: TWO NEW TABLETS, CUT BY HAND.
GOD SAYS WHAT HIS NAME MEANS.
cards: Early in the morning, Moses climbs Sinai again, carrying two blank stone tablets he cut himself. The first pair lie broken at the foot of the mountain, smashed after the golden calf.
The people broke the covenant almost as soon as they made it. If ever there was a moment for God to describe himself as angry, this is it. The cloud comes down.
God passes by, says his own name out loud, and then says what that name means.

teach.h: RACHUM: A MOTHER'S KIND OF LOVE.
teach.b: Here it is, in the King James Bible: "The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin."
Merciful, in Hebrew, is rachum. Lexicons link it to the word for a womb, so some readers hear a mother's kind of love in it. Gracious is giving what isn't earned.
Longsuffering is a picture: erekh appayim, literally long of nostrils.

teach.h: LONG OF NOSTRILS: SLOW TO ANGER.
teach.b: In Hebrew the nose is where anger shows, and God's takes a long, long time to flare. The Psalms put it plainly: slow to anger. Then the great word: hesed.
The King James Bible translates it many ways, mercy, kindness, goodness, lovingkindness, because English has no one word big enough.
Hesed is love that keeps its promises. Loyal, steadfast love, the kind that stays when the other side has given every reason to leave.
The passage goes on to say that guilt isn't simply ignored; it holds mercy and justice together. But look where the weight falls: mercy kept for thousands. And the Bible keeps coming back to it.
Moses quotes it back to God in Numbers.
The Psalms sing it: "The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy."
The prophets Joel and Jonah quote it too. After the calf, the first thing God says about himself is mercy.

how: Some Christians pray with these words from Exodus 34 and Psalm 103, and in Jewish worship the same verses, called the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, are chanted on fast days and the High Holy Days.

o: a warm feeling of affection that comes and goes
loyal love that stays, even after promises are broken
strict justice that weighs every single wrong done

games.q: what's inside God's name — tap the pairs.
p: merciful, linked to the word for womb
long of nostrils: slow to anger
how far the mercy is kept

s: God describes himself this way right after the golden calf
the first tablets lie broken; the first thing God says of himself is merciful and gracious.
hesed has one exact English word
the King James Bible uses mercy, kindness, goodness, lovingkindness. none of them is quite big enough.
this description appears only once in the Bible
Numbers, the Psalms, Joel and Jonah all echo it.

games.q: the people have just broken the covenant with a golden calf. Moses climbs the mountain with new tablets. what's the first thing God says about himself?
o: merciful and gracious, slow to anger.
I will not forgive this people.
games.why: merciful and gracious, longsuffering, abundant in goodness. mercy comes first, right after the calf.

practice: Make your breath long and slow, the way the Hebrew pictures a long nose.

Bring to mind the person most likely to get under your skin, picture the moment it usually happens, and then picture one long breath right there before you answer: not swallowing what's real, just slowing it down.
If you pray, say the words merciful and gracious slowly, as a reminder.

wordCard.voice: Hesed. Hebrew for loyal, steadfast love: love that keeps its promises even after the other side has broken theirs.

orig.note: Hebrew: steadfast, loyal love. Rendered mercy, kindness or lovingkindness in the King James Bible.

carryVoice: Your line: slow to anger. That's week fifty-seven: Sinai, lo tirtzach, the stranger, the calf, the cleft, and hesed. Day three hundred ninety-nine, done.
